in_arabic.name: حمال
in_arabic.meaning: حمال يعني الشخص الذي يحمل الأشياء الثقيلة
in_arabic.long_meaning: حمال هو اسم مشتق من الجذر العربي ح-م-ل، ويعني الشخص الذي يحمل الأشياء الثقيلة. في اللغة العربية، الحمال هو الشخص الذي يتحمل الأثقال والمشاق. وقد ورد هذا الاسم في بعض المصادر العربية القديمة، ويستخدم في بعض الثقافات الإسلامية كاسم للمولود الجديد، معبرًا عن تحمل المسؤوليات والمهام الصعبة في الحياة.

in_urdu.name: حمال
in_urdu.meaning: حمال کا مطلب ہے بھاری چیزیں اٹھانے والا
in_urdu.long_meaning: حمال ایک عربی نام ہے جس کا مطلب ہے بھاری چیزیں اٹھانے والا یا بوجھ اٹھانے والا۔ یہ نام عربی جڑ ح-م-ل سے ماخوذ ہے، جو کہ حمل یا بوجھ کے معنی میں ہے۔ جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی ثقافت میں، یہ نام اہمیت رکھتا ہے کیونکہ یہ تحمل اور صبر کی خوبیوں کی نمائندگی کرتا ہے۔ تاریخی طور پر، حمال ان ممالک میں عام نام رہا ہے جہاں اسلامی ثقافت پھیلی ہوئی ہے، خاص طور پر پاکستان، بھارت، اور دیگر جنوبی ایشیائی ممالک میں۔

in_hindi.name: हमाल
in_hindi.meaning: हमाल का अर्थ है भारी वस्तुएँ उठाने वाला
in_hindi.long_meaning: हमाल एक अरबी नाम है जिसका अर्थ है भारी वस्तुएँ उठाने वाला या भार वाहक। यह नाम अरबी मूल ح-م-ल से निकला है, जो कि भार या बोझ के अर्थ में है। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, यह नाम महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि यह धैर्य और जिम्मेदारी की विशेषताओं को दर्शाता है। यह नाम उन गुणों को महत्व देता है जो एक व्यक्ति को जीवन की चुनौतियों का सामना करने में मदद करते हैं।

in_english.name: Hamal
in_english.meaning: Hamal means the one who carries heavy loads or burdens
in_english.long_meaning: The name Hamal is derived from the Arabic root ح-م-ل (ḥ-m-l), which means to carry or bear. In Islamic tradition, Hamal signifies a person who bears heavy responsibilities and burdens. The name has historical significance in various Muslim cultures, symbolizing strength, endurance, and the ability to face life's challenges. Etymologically, it relates to the concept of carrying or lifting, reflecting qualities of resilience and determination. In modern usage, Hamal is used across different Muslim communities to bestow a sense of capability and fortitude upon the bearer.

data.cultural_impact: Hamal can refer to a person who carries heavy loads or provides transportation in various contexts within Islamic culture. This can include being a camel driver or a laborer, among other occupations. In addition, Hamal can also symbolize resilience and strength, as the person carrying a heavy load endures the physical demands of their work. This concept of carrying weight or supporting others is also reflected in various Islamic traditions, such as the idea of serving and supporting one's community or family.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual realm, the name Hamal carries a deeper meaning. The Arabic root 'h-m-l' not only signifies the act of carrying physical weight, but also the burden of responsibility and moral duty. In Islamic teachings, every individual is responsible for their own moral and ethical actions, and carrying out these responsibilities with integrity and humility can lead to spiritual growth and enlightenment. Hamal can therefore be seen as a name that represents the importance of carrying the weight of one's moral responsibilities, as well as the weight of supporting and caring for others. This principle is encapsulated in the famous Hadith attributed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), which states: "The strong is not the one who overpowers others, but the strong is the one who controls himself in his anger." (Al-Bukhari, Hadith 23) Thus, the name Hamal can serve as a constant reminder of the importance of carrying not only physical burdens, but also the moral and spiritual weight of one's actions and responsibilities.
